model.title: FAA SMS Compliance Review Act of 2026
model.meta: Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee · Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-WA)

summary.text: The bill would require the Federal Aviation Administration to set up an independent expert panel within 60 days of enactment to review and evaluate how the agency runs its safety management system, covering areas such as compliance with agency rules, safety policy, risk management, safety assurance, safety promotion, safety culture, internal audits, staff training, voluntary safety reporting programs, and international aviation safety standards. The panel would include NASA and labor representatives, safety experts, air carrier and industry members, and non-voting representatives from the U.S. ICAO mission and the National Transportation Safety Board. The panel would have limited access to agency records and interviews, and its report would be due within 180 days of its first meeting, with the Administrator required to publish it and respond to its recommendations. The panel would then end, and briefings to Congress would continue for two years.
